+## #785 - Tormach microARC 4: A indexing in the machine file and the PathPilot post
+
+Sources (behaviour only): Tormach TD10749 *Owner's Guide: microARC 4* (1223A),
+TD10552 *4th Axis for M/MX* (0626A), TD10374 *4th Axis, PCNC 1100 / PCNC 770*
+(0626A); the LinuxCNC G-code reference (rotary axes, G93/G94); Tormach's
+PathPilot post-processor guidelines. The issue comment of 2026-11-10 holds
+the three answers in full.
+
+**Indexing only; simultaneous 4-axis refused by name.**
+- **Decided:** A moves alone, as `G0 A..`, after `G53 G0 Z<safe>`, at a
+  section's first motion. An A that changes inside an operation is
+  refused with "simultaneous 4-axis motion ... not confirmed on PathPilot".
+- **Why:** the sources leave both open questions unsettled. TD10749 says
+  nothing about rollover (wrapped A) or feed, and LinuxCNC leaves rollover
+  to each machine's configuration, which PathPilot doesn't publish. An
+  index lands on the same angle under either reading, with the tool up.
+  A wrapped cut would not.
+- **Dropped:** posting wrapped moves under G93 or G94 now. That waits for
+  the PathPilot Hub and the user's hardware, in #796.
+
+**The A word is read through the tool axis, not the letters.**
+- **Decided:** the post computes the tool axis from the stream's A/B/C
+  (the pose law, Rz(C)·Ry(B)·Rx(A)·Z). It accepts any axis with no X
+  component and takes a = atan2(sin, cos) in -180..180. C must be 0.
+- **Why:** the 3+2 tilt stores canonical letters (A in -90..90), so the
+  face underneath arrives as A0 B180. An A about X reaches it as A180,
+  and refusing it as "a B" would be wrong.
+- **Limit found:** the app's machine check (`machine::check`) judges the
+  letters themselves and does no IK. A0 B180 is therefore still refused
+  there ("states no B axis") before the post is reached. The test part
+  uses the opposite pair A-90 / A90 instead of 0 / 180, and the gap is
+  filed as #797.
+
+**The indexed frame.**
+- **Decided:** each tilted tip is posted relative to the work offset,
+  turned by -a about X, so the tool stands up Z.
+- **Why:** this needs WCS Y0 Z0 on the A centerline. Nothing in the
+  stream can check that, so it is an operator note at the first index and
+  a README setup step.
+- **Dropped:** a machine-file centerline offset. The setup states the
+  offset; the machine file doesn't.
+
+**Direction sense = the sign of the rotary's `axis` vector.**
+- **Decided:** `[1, 0, 0]` follows RS-274 / ISO 841: a + A turns the tool
+  right-handed about +X relative to the part, so the stream's angle posts
+  as itself. `[-1, 0, 0]` posts it negated.
+- **Why:** the parser refuses a rotary `direction: -1` ("a reversed rotary
+  is not supported"), and the vector is already the rotary's stated
+  geometry.
+- **Not confirmed:** the microARC 4's real sense isn't in TD10749. The
+  test kit's first step checks it with an MDI `G0 A90`.
+
+**No clamp code.**
+- **Decided:** the post writes no clamp code and adds an operator note.
+- **Why:** none of the three guides names an M-code. The microARC 4 (a
+  harmonic drive) has no clamp at all. The older tables clamp by hand and
+  must be released to rotate.
+
+**Travel -360..360, rates unstated.**
+- **Decided:** the machine file states travel -360..360 and no rates.
+- **Why:** TD10749 states neither a travel stop nor a rate. The tool angle
+  is always in -180..180, so the travel never binds. A machine stating less
+  travel is refused by name. The unstated-limit law keeps the rates absent
+  rather than invented (TD10374's 4 RPM is the older worm tables, not the
+  microARC).
+
+**Upright sections state A0 on a 4th-axis machine.**
+- **Decided:** a program for a machine with an A always writes `G0 A..` at
+  its first motion, `A0` for an upright job. A machine without an A writes
+  no A at all, so every existing golden is byte-identical.
+- **Why:** the control's A after the last run is unknown.
+
+**One file, the 770MX + microARC 4.**
+- **Decided:** a separate machine file rather than an option on the
+  existing ones.
+- **Why:** the schema has no option concept. Other mills follow the same
+  pattern by copying their file and adding the one rotary part.
+
+**Parser fix found on the way.**
+- **What:** `parse_mch`'s head search stopped at the first part with no
+  children (`get("parts")?`). A rotary leaf listed before the head lost the
+  spindle range, belt ranges, rigid tapping and coolant, silently.
+- **Fix:** the search now passes leaves over. It is pinned by
+  `the_microarc_machine_states_an_a_about_x`.
+
+**A is restated after every G30 and at every section (review of PR #798).**
+- **Decided:** the post forgets the A it holds (`aNow = null`) when it
+  writes `G30`, and again at every section end. Every section therefore
+  opens with `G53 G0 Z<safe>` / `G0 A..`, even on the same face as the
+  section before, with or without a tool change between.
+- **Why:** a `G30` with no axis words moves every axis to the stored G30
+  position (LinuxCNC, params 5181-5189), A included, and the app re-issues
+  the tool (so `G30 / T.. M6`) before every operation. Two operations on
+  the same face posted the second with no `G0 A..`, cutting wherever G30
+  left the table. The same-tool continuation (no G30) moves nothing in A,
+  but a section boundary is where an operator may stop (M0/M1, a probe
+  check) and jog, so the cheaper rule - keep A across same-tool sections -
+  was dropped: one extra Z lift is the whole cost.
+- **Dropped:** changing the `G30` itself so it leaves A alone (axis words
+  on a G30 add an intermediate-point move and change PathPilot's own
+  tool-change convention for every Tormach program), and a swept-radius check before an index (filed as a
+  follow-up; the kit README now asks the operator to confirm it).

+# Tormach microARC 4 kit: `microarc_test_part.nc`
+
+**Machine:** Tormach 770MX (PathPilot v2.7.2 or later) with the microARC 4 as the A axis (Settings > 4th Axis Rotary > "4" 4th Axis").
+**Tests:** issue #785. The PathPilot post indexes A between operations: Z goes straight up (`G53 G0 Z0`), then A turns on its own line (`G0 A..`), then an ordinary 3-axis cut. No A word ever rides a cutting move.
+**Built by CamCraft:** `microarc_test_part.camproj` is the project, and `microarc_test_part.nc` is exactly what it posts (pinned by `crates/app/tests/microarc_test_part.rs`).
+
+## The part
+3/4" round bar, 6061 aluminium or 360 brass. Every cut is shallow, and the whole program runs in a few minutes, mostly tool changes and indexes.
+
+| Op | Index | Tool | Cut |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| FLAT A-90 | `G0 A-90` | T1, 1/4" flat end mill | a flat 0.015" deep, one 1/4" pass from X-0.125 to X-0.875 (the tool centre runs X-0.25 to X-0.75), on the side that faced the back (+Y) |
+| FLAT A90 | `G0 A90` | T1 | the same flat on the side that faced you (front, -Y), opposite the first |
+| CROSS SLOT A0 | `G0 A0` | T2, 1/8" flat end mill | a 1/8" groove across the top at X-0.5, 0.020" deep in two 0.010" steps (it runs out both sides of the bar) |
+
+Speeds are 6000 rpm (T1) and 8000 rpm (T2), both in the high belt range (the program says so before each spindle start). Feeds are 15 ipm and 8 ipm, with flood coolant (M8). The program doesn't number your tools for you: set T1 and T2 in the tool table, or edit the `T.. M6` / `G43 H..` lines to your own numbers (for example your T31 1/4" 3-flute).
+
+**The continuous op is not in this program.** A wrapped pass around the diameter turns A during the cut. PathPilot's handling of that (rollover, combined feed) isn't confirmed yet, so CamCraft refuses it, naming the operation, and writes no file. (The PathPilot post refuses it as "simultaneous 4-axis motion ... not confirmed on PathPilot". On this part the program check names it first, because the pass also goes under the bar, #797.) Its test joins this kit with the follow-up, #796.
+
+## The setup
+- **Stock:** 3/4" bar, at least 2.5" long, in the microARC chuck with **1.5" sticking out** (1.25" minimum: the cuts reach X-0.875).
+- **Units:** inch (`G20`).
+- **Work offset G54:**
+  - **X0 at the free end face** of the bar.
+  - **Y0 and Z0 on the A axis centerline.** Z0 is the centre of the bar, not its top: the top of the bar is Z0.375. Find Y0 by indicating both sides of the bar, and Z0 by touching the top and subtracting 0.375". The program's turns are only right if Y0 Z0 lie exactly on the centerline. The program says so in a comment at the first index.
+- **A0:** mark a line on the top of the bar at A0. The cross slot lands on that line, and the flats land 90 degrees either side of it.
+- **No clamp code:** the microARC 4 has no clamp, and the program writes none.
+
+## Safety first
+1. **Check the A direction before anything else.** In MDI, with the tool well clear, run `G0 A90` from A0. The side of the bar that faced you (the front) must come to the **top**. If the back comes up instead, **stop**: the direction sense is reversed for this post, so tell us on the issue and don't run the program.
+2. **Check the collet nut clears the chuck.** At X-0.875 (the inner end of the flats) the ER20 nut must clear the chuck jaws with the tool at Z0.36. Keep at least 1" of tool stick-out from the nut.
+3. **Check the swept radius at the safe Z.** Before every `G0 A..` the program lifts Z to the top of travel (`G53 G0 Z0`), and that is the only clearance it gives: nothing in CamCraft checks the part, the chuck and its jaws against the tool while A turns. Before the first A move, jog Z to the top (`G53 G0 Z0`) and confirm the tool tip (and the collet nut) clears the radius the part, chuck and jaws sweep as A turns a full revolution. On this 3/4" bar it does with room to spare; a bigger part, a bigger chuck or a long tool may not. If it doesn't clear, don't run the program.
+4. **Know your G30 position's A.** Every tool change starts with `G30`, and the program ends with one. A `G30` with no axis words takes **every** axis to the stored G30 position, A included, so A may turn there, together with X and Y (Z is already at the top of travel when it starts). The program never trusts A after a `G30`: every operation states its own `G0 A..` again after its `T.. M6`. Check the A your G30 position holds (set it with A0 if you can), and make sure the tool clears the part there too.
+5. **Air-cut first.** Shift G54 Z up 1" (so Z0 sits 1" above the centerline), and run at 25% feed and rapid override with single-block on. Watch every `G0 A..` line: Z must already be at the top (`G53 G0 Z0` on the line before), and A must turn only on its own line.
+6. Only then cut, aluminium or brass, with a hand on feed hold and E-stop. This is a test program, not a production part.
+
+## Checklist
+1. The program loads in PathPilot with no error. If it doesn't, send the line and the message.
+2. Before the first index there are two comments (WCS on the A centerline, no clamp code), and then `G53 G0 Z0`, `G0 A-90`.
+3. Every `G0 A..` line is preceded by `G53 G0 Z0`, and A turns with Z at the top. Every operation has its own `G0 A..` after its `T.. M6`, even when the A is the same as the last one (after the `G30`, A is wherever the G30 position put it).
+4. **FLAT A-90:** the flat is cut on the side that faced the back, about 0.21" wide and 3/4" long, from 1/8" to 7/8" in from the end.
+5. **FLAT A90:** the second flat is exactly opposite the first. Measure across the flats: 0.720" (0.750 - 2 x 0.015).
+6. **CROSS SLOT A0:** the groove crosses your A0 line 1/2" from the end, 1/8" wide and 0.020" deep, square to the bar.
+7. The program ends with Z up, G30 and M30. The last operation runs at A0, but the final `G30` then takes A to your stored G30 position's A: A is left there, which is 0 only if your G30 position holds A0. Note where A ended.
+8. Total run time is a few minutes.
+
+Send back the PathPilot version, the result of each step, the across-flats measurement, and a photo of the part.
